Πνεύματος στερέωσις καὶ "εἰς ἄνδρα τέλειον" ἀναδρομὴ ἀναλόγως ταῖς ἑκάστου
σπουδαῖς τε καὶ προθυμίαις χορηγουμένη; 259 Θεοῦ γεώργιον, Θεοῦ οἰκοδομή ἐστε.
Ἐπειδὴ Χριστὸς ἡμᾶς ἐξηγόρασεν τῷ τιμίῳ αὐτοῦ αἵματι τὸν τῆς σαρκὸς ἀνατλὰς

ἑτέρων ὀνομαζόμεθα ἀλλὰ μόνου Χριστοῦ ὃς καὶ κυριεύει ἡμῶν. Ὡς σοφὸς ἀρχιτέκτων

Ἐπειδὴ οἶκον ὠνόμασεν Θεοῦ τοὺς πεπιστευκότας, θεμέλιον εἰκότως ὀνομάζει
Χριστόν· καὶ πολλοὶ μὲν διδάσκαλοι γεγόνασι παρὰ Κορινθίοις, αὐχεῖ δὲ ὁ Παῦλος τὸ

κατὰ τὸν βίον. ἐπεὶ οὖν πεφυσίωνταί τινες ἀπόντος μου καὶ νομίζουσι διὰ τοῦτό με
ἀπολιμπάνεσθαι ὡς δεδιότα τοῦ ἐλθεῖν αὐτοῖς εἰς λόγους, ὅπερ οὐχ οὕτως ἔχει, ἥξω
θέλοντος καὶ ἐπιτρέποντος Θεοῦ. Ἐλεύσομαι δὲ ταχέως πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἐὰν ὁ Κύριος θελήσῃ.
Ἐπηγγείλατο μὲν ἀφίξεσθαι πλὴν οὐ πάντως, ἀλλ' ὡς πρέπον ἦν ἐπιεικῶς προσθεὶς τὸ
ἀναγκαῖον τό Ἐὰν ὁ Κύριος θελήσῃ· δεῖ γὰρ ἡμᾶς οὐχ ἑτέρως ἢ φρονεῖν ἢ λέγειν ἢ ὧδέ
τε καὶ μόνος. Καὶ γνώσομαι οὐ τὸν λόγον τῶν πεφυσιωμένων, ἀλλὰ τὴν δύναμιν. Τίς ἡ

γε τῆς θεοπνεύστου γραφῆς ἁπλὴ μέν ἐστι καὶ κατειθισμένη, πλουσίως γεμὴν ὀνίνησι
καὶ ἀποφέρει λαμπρῶς εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν ἀληθῆ τοῦ 261 κατὰ φύσιν ὄντος Θεοῦ· ἀποτελεῖ
δὲ πρὸς τοῦτο καὶ παντὸς ἀξια[γασ]τοῦ πράγματος ἐπιμελητάς· οὗ δὴ γεγονότος,

γὰρ ἐν λόγῳ ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἀλλ' ἐν δυνάμει· τὸ δέ Ἐν δυνάμει νοήσεις, εἰ μὲν

pass_a_gloss: [from u01 close: ... nourishing the mind of the one who believed so that it might appear fruitful?] What but the growth (αὔξησις) the from Christ, or through Spirit (Πνεύματος) firming (στερέωσις) and 'to man perfect (ἄνδρα τέλειον)' running-up (ἀναδρομή) proportionally (ἀναλόγως) to the zeal (σπουδαῖς) and readiness (προθυμίαις) of each being supplied (χορηγουμένη)? Of God field (γεώργιον), of God building (οἰκοδομή) you are. Since Christ bought us out (ἐξηγόρασεν) with his precious (τιμίῳ) blood, the of-flesh death having endured (ἀνατλάς), of the one who bought (ἀγοράσαντος) by all means we are, not of others, even if have become toward us some ministers (διάκονοι) and reconcilers (διαλλάκται) and mediators (μεσίται) and initiators (μυσταγωγοί) of the from-him grace (χάριτος); wherefore not of others are we named but of Christ alone who also is lord over (κυριεύει) us. As wise architect (ἀρχιτέκτων) foundation (θεμέλιον) I have laid. Since he named house (οἶκον) of God the ones who have believed, foundation fittingly he names Christ; and many indeed teachers came to be among Corinthians, but boasts (αὐχεῖ) Paul the being first of the others, and as a firstfruit (ἀπαρχή) of those who evangelised to them the mystery of Christ, who is foundation unshakeable (ἀκατάσειστος), holding up (ἀνέχων) the ones being built upon him, and temples (ναούς) showing, being fitted together (συναρμολογουμένους) with one another through faith and by the grace of the Holy Spirit coming together (συμβαίνοντος) into same-soulness (ὁμοψυχίαν); about this foundation was saying God and Father through prophet 'Behold I cast into the foundations of Zion stone costly (πολυτελῆ) cornerstone (ἀκρογωνιαῖον) honoured (ἔντιμον), into the foundations of her, and the one believing on him not at all will be put to shame (καταισχυνθῇ).' To have laid then Paul very well says the foundation himself, and others to be able to work upon and build, not however still to lay down also another beside the already lying, who is Jesus Christ; 'for not is other name under heaven given among men in which must we be saved (σωθῆναι).' 'For one God and Father, from whom all things and we into him, and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom all things and we through him, and he is the head (κεφαλή) of the body of the church (ἐκκλησίας).' If someone then denies (ἀρνεῖται) the foundation and refuses (παραιτεῖται) the rock (πέτραν), not he builds on it but into the sand (ἄμμον); for this very reason also very easily he will be shaken down (κατασεισθήσεται); for what not holds up Christ, this by all means will be moved, not firm having the standing (στάσιν). As not coming but of me to you were puffed up (ἐφυσιώθησαν) some. Since some were in Corinth thinking to suffice themselves and not to need teachers, and to surpass in wisdom of worldly good-tongue (εὐγλωττίας) Paul; and through this were puffed up to disdain (ὑπεροψίαν) rising up against (κατεξανιστάμενοι) the others, yet not blameless (ἀνεπίληπτοι) in life. Since then some have been puffed up, me being absent, and think through this me to stay behind (ἀπολιμπάνεσθαι) as fearing to come to them into words, which is not so, I will come, God willing (θέλοντος) and permitting (ἐπιτρέποντος). I will come but quickly to you, if the Lord wills (θελήσῃ). He promised to arrive, yet not absolutely (οὐ πάντως), but as fitting was, reasonably (ἐπιεικῶς) having added the necessary 'If the Lord wills'; for must we not otherwise either think or say than thus and alone (μόνος). And I will know not the word of the puffed-up ones, but the power (δύναμιν). What the benefit (ὄνησις) of diction brilliant (λαμπρᾶς) having of the goods nothing, such as is that of the Greeks (ἑλλήνων)? But that of the God-breathed (θεοπνεύστου) scripture is simple (ἁπλή) and customary (κατειθισμένη), richly however benefits and carries off brilliantly into knowledge true (ἐπίγνωσιν ἀληθῆ) of the by-nature (κατὰ φύσιν) being God; renders also toward this of every admirable (ἀξιαγάστου) matter careful ones (ἐπιμελητάς); which having happened, would be enriched (καταπλουτήσειεν) someone also of the through-Spirit gifts (χαρισμάτων) with the worth-receiving (ἀξιόληπτον) grace; for not in word the kingdom of the heavens, but in power; the 'In power' you will understand, if on the holy apostles themselves it is carried, as in strength (ἰσχύϊ) and working (ἐνεργείᾳ) the through the Spirit, according to which they are also wonder-workers (θαυματουργοί); but if on ourselves, as in power of life holy and sincere (εἰλικρινοῦς) you will receive (ἐκδέξῃ) the said. What do you want? With rod (ῥάβδῳ) shall I come to you or [in love? — completed from head of u02-rem-early]
pass_b_english: And what is the growth that comes from Christ, if not the strengthening given through the Spirit and the rising up “to a mature man” (Ephesians 4:13), granted in proportion to each one’s diligence and eagerness?

“You are God’s field, God’s building” (1 Corinthians 3:9). Since Christ redeemed us with his precious blood (1 Peter 1:19), having endured the death of the flesh, we surely belong to him who bought us, and to no others, even if some have become for us ministers, reconcilers, mediators, and teachers of the mysteries of the grace that comes from him. That is why we are named after no others, but after Christ alone, who is also our Lord.

“Like a wise master builder I laid a foundation” (1 Corinthians 3:10). Since he called believers the house of God, he fittingly names Christ the foundation. There had been many teachers among the Corinthians, but Paul boasts that he was the first of them all, a kind of firstfruits among those who preached to them the mystery of Christ. Christ is the unshakable foundation. He holds up those who are built upon him and shows them to be temples, fitted together with one another through faith (Ephesians 2:21) and brought together into one mind by the grace of the Holy Spirit. Of this foundation God the Father spoke through the prophet: “Behold, I lay in the foundations of Zion a costly stone, a precious cornerstone, in her foundations; and whoever believes in him shall not be put to shame” (Isaiah 28:16).

So Paul says, and very rightly, that he himself laid the foundation, and that others can work on it and build upon it, but can no longer lay another beside the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ (1 Corinthians 3:11). “For there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved” (Acts 4:12). “For there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things, and we for him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we through him” (1 Corinthians 8:6), “and he is the head of the body, the church” (Colossians 1:18). If anyone, then, denies the foundation and refuses the rock, he does not build on it but on the sand (Matthew 7:24–27), and so he will very easily be shaken down. For what Christ does not hold up will surely be moved, since it has no firm footing.

“Some have become puffed up, as though I were not coming to you” (1 Corinthians 4:18). There were some in Corinth who thought themselves sufficient and in no need of teachers, and who thought they surpassed Paul in the wisdom of worldly eloquence. For this reason they were puffed up to the point of contempt and rose up against the others, though they themselves were not blameless in their lives. Paul means: Since some have become puffed up while I am away, and think that I stay away because I am afraid to come and face them in argument, which is not so, I will come, if God wills and permits.

“But I will come to you soon, if the Lord wills” (1 Corinthians 4:19). He promised to come, yet not without condition. As was fitting, he modestly added the needful words, “if the Lord wills.” For we must think and speak in this way, and in no other.

“And I will find out not the talk of those who are puffed up, but their power” (1 Corinthians 4:19). What is the use of brilliant speech that holds nothing good, such as the speech of the pagan Greeks? But the speech of the inspired Scripture is simple and ordinary, yet it gives rich profit and carries one splendidly to the true knowledge of him who is God by nature. It also makes people diligent in every admirable work. And when this has come about, a person may be enriched with the grace of the gifts given through the Spirit, a grace worth receiving. “For the kingdom of heaven is not in word but in power” (1 Corinthians 4:20). As for “in power,” if it is said of the holy apostles themselves, you will understand it as the strength and working that comes through the Spirit, by which they also work wonders. But if it is said of us, you will take it to mean the power of a holy and sincere life.
“What do you wish? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love?” (1 Corinthians 4:21).
